transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

[Heading: Blocked or misaligned burner cap/ports]
A lazy yellow flame with black soot usually means the burner isn't getting enough air or the gas/air mix is wrong. This is most often caused by a burner cap that is slightly misaligned, wet from washing, or clogged with food debris in its small ports. Please switch off the gas supply to be safe. Lift off the metal burner cap and the inner crown on that back burner. Check that they are dry, clean (especially the small holes around the edge), and sit perfectly flat when replaced. If they look clear but the issue continues, check that your pan base is completely flat and free of external soot. Let me know if cleaning or reseating them fixes the flame colour.
[Safety panel] If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.

I've had a look and the cap seems to be sitting properly, though there are some burnt spills around it. Your safety note made me think I should mention that I've noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. Should I be worried about that?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.
